Compute MAE and RMSE from a fitted Poisson or linear model

Source: R/model_metrics.R
mysterycall_model_metrics.Rd

Extracts fitted values and the observed response from a fitted model and returns mean absolute error and root-mean-square error. Works with mysterycall_poisson_model() results, bare glm, glmerMod, or lm objects.

Usage

mysterycall_model_metrics(model)

Arguments

model

A mysterycall_poisson_model result, or a glm, glmerMod, or lm object.

Value

A named list with two numeric scalar elements:

mae

Numeric scalar (or NA_real_). Mean absolute error: mean(|observed - fitted|). Measures average prediction error in the original response units.

rmse

Numeric scalar (or NA_real_). Root-mean-square error: sqrt(mean((observed - fitted)^2)). Penalizes large errors more heavily than MAE.

Both elements are NA_real_ when fitted values cannot be extracted (e.g., model fitting failed or an unsupported class was passed).

See also

mysterycall_poisson_model() which produces compatible model objects; mysterycall_select_best_model() for AIC/BIC-based selection.

Other outcomes: .as_positive_logical(), .disp_rate_ci(), .fmt_model_pval(), .fmt_pvalue(), .me_find_mf_col(), .me_mf_to_orig(), .wait_stats(), .wilson_ci(), mysterycall_acceptance_rate(), mysterycall_bootstrap_ci(), mysterycall_irr_plot(), mysterycall_marginal_effects(), mysterycall_plot_distribution(), mysterycall_plot_effect(), mysterycall_plot_emmeans_full(), mysterycall_plot_emmeans_interaction(), mysterycall_plot_inclexcl(), mysterycall_plot_residuals(), mysterycall_plot_sjplot_interaction(), mysterycall_plot_stacked_bar(), mysterycall_poisson_model(), mysterycall_screen_interactions(), mysterycall_select_best_model(), mysterycall_wait_time_summary(), print.mysterycall_poisson_model()

Examples

m <- glm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, family = gaussian())
mysterycall_model_metrics(m)
#> $mae
#> [1] 2.340642
#> 
#> $rmse
#> [1] 2.949163
#>
